intro_html: Filipino chicken adobo is proof that a handful of pantry staples can make something unforgettable. Vinegar, soy, garlic, and time do all the work, and you land at 64 grams of protein per bowl for about $3.35 (at everyday cost). One batch makes 14 servings, so a couple of cheap bottles feed you for a week and a half.
cost_closing_html: About $3.35 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each serving delivers 64 grams of protein and 561 calories, big protein for barely two dollars.
upsell_html: Simple ingredients, huge payoff. That's the whole idea of eating well without overspending. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: This whole dish rides on vinegar and soy sauce you can buy dirt cheap, so it keeps the cost per bowl low.
Onions and garlic keep for weeks in a cool spot, so buy the bag, not the single and always have them on hand.
When chicken breast is high, use thighs instead. Adobo actually tastes better with them, and they're usually cheaper.
make_it: Add the chicken, white vinegar, soy sauce, brown sugar, sliced onion, and garlic to the slow cooker.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 hours until the chicken is tender and soaked with flavor.
Drop the broccoli florets in for the last 30 minutes so they cook but stay firm.
Shred the chicken in the pot and let it soak up the tangy sauce for a few minutes.
Spoon it over white rice with plenty of that dark, salty-sour sauce.

head.description: A high-protein Filipino meal prep. Fourteen servings at about 561 calories and 64 grams of protein for roughly $3.35 each (at everyday cost).
